Counsel for Petitioner :- M.K. Singh Bhardwaj Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.,Sudeep Kumar,Sanjeev Pandey Hon'ble Vivek Chaudhary,J.
Hon'ble Narendra Kumar Johari,J.
Supplementary affidavit filed by learned counsel for the petitioners today is taken on record.
Heard learned counsel for the petitioners, learned counsel for the private respondents, learned AGA for the State-respondents and perused the record.

By means of this writ petition, the petitioner has sought quashing of the First Information Report dated 16.12.2021 registered as case Crime No.451 of 2021, under Sections 498A, 313, 307, 354, 427,
504, 506 IPC and 3/4 of D.P. Act, P.S. Gomti Nagar Extension, District Lucknow.

sentences.text:
On 4.7.2023, this Court had passed the following order:
"Heard learned counsel for the petitioners and learned A.G.A. who appears on behalf of State-respondents and perused the impugned F.I.R. as well as material brought on record.

This petition has been filed by the petitioners for the following main prayer:-
"1) Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of Certiorari to quash the impugned First Information Report dated 16.12.2021 registered as FIR/ Case Crime No.451 of 2021, under Sections 498-A, 313, 307, 354, 427, 504, 506 of IPC and Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station Gomti Nagar, District Lucknow, as annexed as Annexure No.1 to this writ petition."

Learned counsel for the petitioners says that an amount of Rs. 3 lacs, which was due as arrears towards maintenance has been given to the respondent no. 4 by way of bank draft as provided in this Court's order dated 7.6.2023.
Sri Sanjeev Pandey, who appears for the respondent no. 4, does not dispute payment of arrears of maintenance having been made to the respondent no. 4.
Learned counsel for the respondent no. 4, however, says that till date no order has been passed with regard to sending the matter to the mediation and conciliation centre of this Court.

He further submitted that since the respondent no. 4 has expressed her willingness to sent her matter to the mediation and conciliation centre of this Court for an attempt to be made to settle the dispute amicably, therefore, an appropriate order should also be made by this Court.

Learned counsel for the petitioners is ready to deposit a sum of Rs. 50,000/- by bank draft in the name of Senior Registrar, Mediation and Conciliation Centre, High Court Lucknow Bench, Lucknow within two weeks to show his bona fide to settle the dispute amicably.

If the amount of Rs. 50,000/- is deposited by the petitioner no. 2 by way of bank draft in the name of Senior Registrar, Mediation and Conciliation Centre, High Court Lucknow Bench, Lucknow then on the next date of listing, the matter will be referred to the Mediation and Conciliation Centre.

It is also made clear that out of Rs. 50,000/- a sum of Rs. 25,000/- shall be payable to the respondent No.4- Smt. Shipu Srivastava on her first appearance before the Mediation and Conciliation Centre of this Court and Rs.20,000/- shall be payable to the respondent No.4- Smt. Shipu Srivastava on completion of mediation proceedings between the parties.

The remaining amount i.e. Rs.5000/-
shall go to the Mediation Centre as mediation fee.
It is clarified that the amount so deposited by the petitioner no.2 shall be adjusted in the final settlement arrive at between the parties, if any.
List this case on 25.7.2023 showing the name of Sri Sanjeev Pandey, Advocate as counsel for the respondent no. 4.

On the next date of listing, Mediation and Conciliation Centre of this Court shall submit a report to clarify the fact that the amount of Rs. 50,000/- has been deposited by the Smt. entities.text: Smt. Veena Srivastava And Others vs State Of U.P. Thru. Secy. Deptt. Of Home
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: petitioner no. 2 or not.

Till the next date of listing, the petitioners shall not be arrested in pursuance of the impugned F.I.R.
subject to the cooperation of the petitioners in the investigation and subject to the payment of Rs.
50,000/- by the petitioner no. 2 by way of bank draft in the name of Senior Registrar, Mediation and Conciliation Centre, High Court Lucknow Bench, Lucknow. "

The report of the Mediation Centre of this Court dated 21.5.2024 is on record,
according to which, the parties have settled their dispute amicably by way of settlement/agreement.
According to the terms of the settlement/agreement, which is enclosed with the Mediation Centre's report, parties have decided to withdraw all the cases filed by them against each other.

Learned counsel for the opposite party no.4 did not dispute to the same rather he has given the consent that the parties have settled their dispute and the opposite party no.4 has not any grievance in future also.
As the parties have settled their dispute amicably, we see no reason to allow the investigation to proceed in pursuance to the impugned FIR.
We, accordingly, quash the FIR, all proceedings/investigation which may have been held consequent thereto are also quashed and the writ petition is allowed.
As per settlement-agreement entered between the parties, Mediation and Conciliation Centre of this Court is directed to release all the amount in favour of opposite party no. 4.

Learned AGA shall communicate this order to the court concerned as well as investigating officer.
.
(Narendra Kumar Johari, J.) (Vivek Chaudhary,J.) Order Date :- 30.9.2024
